questions.q: A client retries the same request three times after a timeout. With which method does the server end up in the same state as with a single request?
questions.explanation: PUT is idempotent: replacing the resource three times leaves the same result as once. POST may create three resources. A PATCH that increments a counter adds one on every attempt. An empty body doesn't make POST idempotent.

questions.q: The API reports that the requested resource doesn't exist. Which code fits?
questions.explanation: 404 is a client error: it asked for something that doesn't exist. 500 blames the server. 301 is a redirect. 201 means something was created.

questions.q: The server is overloaded and can't handle requests for a while. Which code does it return?
questions.explanation: 503 Service Unavailable signals a temporary server failure. 404 and 400 blame the client. 302 is a redirect.

questions.q: Which method is used to read a resource without modifying it?
questions.explanation: GET is safe: it doesn't change state. POST and PUT write, DELETE deletes.

questions.q: A client times out on a PUT and retries it. Why is that safe, and would the same retry be safe with POST?
rubric: States that PUT is idempotent: repeating it leaves the same state
Explains that POST is not idempotent and a retry may create a duplicate
Names a way to make POST retries safe (for example an idempotency key) or says it needs one
